about.title: About MailCopilot
about.sentryHint: Includes crash reports, performance measurements, product usage events (which features are used, which AI provider and model, the estimated cost of a request) and a random install identifier that links your sessions. Message content, subjects and folder names are not collected: nothing that is sent is built from them, with one exception — when a quick action turns a draft down as too long, that refusal is counted with one of six declared length bands, never the text and never its exact length. Addresses and file paths are removed automatically from the error text a mail server returns, wherever they can be recognised. The only address that is sent is the one you type into the feedback form below yourself, so that you can get a reply.

telemetryConsent.title: Send diagnostic data?
telemetryConsent.intro: MailCopilot can send diagnostic and usage data so that crashes and slowdowns can be found and fixed. It never contains the content of your mail, but it does include a random identifier for this installation, so it is not fully anonymous. Nothing is sent unless you choose to allow it. Your mail and the AI assistant work the same either way — if you decline, the feedback form in Settings becomes a link to our website.
telemetryConsent.sentTitle: If you allow it, MailCopilot sends:

sent.errors: Errors and crashes: the type of error and the stack trace showing where in the code it happened
sent.versions: The MailCopilot version, your operating system and its version
sent.performance: How long operations took — mail synchronisation, search, sending, AI requests
sent.usage: Which features you used and how often — search, writing mail, AI, rules, templates, snoozing — plus the AI provider and model used and the estimated cost of a request
sent.aiKeyStore: Actions on the store where your AI keys are kept: which provider, whether the key was being read, saved or removed, and how it went — including whether a key was found there. The key itself is never sent.
sent.setup: Basic setup facts: how many accounts you have, the kind of mail service (for example Gmail or Outlook), the sign-in method, the interface language and the theme
sent.installId: A random identifier for this installation, created on first run. It is not tied to your email address, but it does link the data from your different sessions to the same installation.

never.bodies: Message bodies, subjects and your folder names are not collected: only the general kind of folder, such as Inbox or Trash, appears in the data, and nothing we send is built from your text — with one narrow exception. When a quick action in the compose window turns a draft down for being longer than it accepts, that refusal is counted together with one of six declared size bands, such as 8k–12k characters: not the length itself, not a single word of the draft, and only at the moment of that refusal. The one text we do not write ourselves is a mail server's error message; addresses and file paths are removed from it automatically before it is sent, wherever they can be recognised
never.addresses: Email addresses, yours or anyone else's. The only exception is the feedback form in Settings → About: an address you type there yourself is sent along with your message, so that you can get a reply
never.searchQueries: What you type into search — only the length of the query and the number of results are counted
never.aiPrompts: The text of AI requests and answers

telemetryConsent.changeLater: You can change this decision at any time: Settings → About.

translate.label: Allow translating received messages and your own drafts with AI
translate.help: Adds a Translate control above the message you are reading. Nothing is translated automatically — a provider is only called when you press it, and the original is always one click away. The translation is shown as plain text and never replaces the stored message. The same control appears in the compose window for a draft you are writing: MailCopilot sends only the text you wrote yourself — a quote, a forward header or a signature it recognises stays out of the request and comes back unchanged. That recognition is not complete: some quoting styles used by other mail apps carry no marker MailCopilot can see, and on such a draft the whole body is sent. Nothing is translated on its own here either: the result appears in a review panel beside your draft and replaces it only if you choose to. Off by default; enabled per account.

aiDestination.confirmTitle: Change where AI requests are sent?
aiDestination.confirmMessage: AI requests are about to be sent through a different address.
aiDestination.confirmDetail: Continue only if you entered this address yourself. If you did not just change the AI settings, choose Cancel.
aiDestination.endpointRisk: Every AI request to this address carries your API key, so whoever runs it receives that key and everything the assistant sends.
aiDestination.endpointRiskCleartext: Every AI request to this address carries your API key, so whoever runs it receives that key and everything the assistant sends. The address starts with http:// rather than https://, so those requests are not encrypted: anyone on the network path — including any proxy — can read them as well.
aiDestination.endpointRiskInactive: This address is used only when the AI provider is set to an OpenAI-compatible service, which is not the provider in use right now. If that provider is selected later, every AI request to this address will carry your API key, so whoever runs it would receive that key and everything the assistant sends.
aiDestination.endpointRiskInactiveCleartext: This address is used only when the AI provider is set to an OpenAI-compatible service, which is not the provider in use right now. If that provider is selected later, every AI request to this address will carry your API key, so whoever runs it would receive that key and everything the assistant sends. The address also starts with http:// rather than https://, so those requests would not be encrypted: anyone on the network path — including any proxy — could read them as well.
aiDestination.proxyRisk: Every AI request is routed through this proxy, so whoever runs it sees which addresses you contact, and how much and how often. They can read your API key and the messages themselves only if the proxy intercepts encrypted connections with a certificate this computer trusts.
aiDestination.proxyRiskCleartext: Every AI request is routed through this proxy, and the AI endpoint address starts with http:// rather than https://, so those requests are not encrypted. Whoever runs the proxy can therefore read your API key and the messages themselves, not merely see which addresses you contact.
aiDestination.declined: The new address for AI requests was not confirmed, so the previous one is still in use.
aiDestination.invalid: This is not a usable address for AI requests. Enter a full http:// or https:// address; the AI endpoint address must not contain a query string or a #fragment.
aiDestination.busy: A confirmation of the AI request address is already open. Answer it first, then try again.
